article.headline: Freshmen Diaz, Mobley lead No. 17 Ohio State women to 93-49 victory over Fairleigh Dickinson
article.description: — Freshmen Adriana Diaz and Sydney Mobley each scored a season-high 18 points and No. 17 Ohio State cruised to a 93-49 victory over Fairleigh Dickinson on Sunday.
article.linkText: Freshmen Diaz, Mobley lead No. 17 Ohio State women to 93-49 victory over Fairleigh Dickinson

categories.description: Fairleigh Dickinson Knights @ Ohio State Buckeyes

event.description: Fairleigh Dickinson Knights @ Ohio State Buckeyes

keywords: Fairleigh Dickinson Knights @ Ohio State Buckeyes
article.story: COLUMBUS, Ohio -- — Freshmen Adriana Diaz and Sydney Mobley each scored a season-high 18 points and No. 17 Ohio State cruised to a 93-49 victory over Fairleigh Dickinson on Sunday. Diaz made 6 of 9 shots with two 3-pointers and all four of her free throws for the Buckeyes (4-1), adding five rebounds and four assists. Mobley came off the bench to make 7 of 10 shots with two 3-pointers. She hit both of her foul shots and grabbed five rebounds. Jaloni Cambridge totaled 15 points, seven assists and five boards for Ohio State, which was coming off an 87-55 home loss to No. 4 Connecticut. Kylee Kitts posted a double-double with 13 points and 11 rebounds. Reese Downey hit five 3-pointers and scored 17 to pace the Knights (2-3). Downey sank a 3-pointer to give Fairleigh Dickinson a 3-2 lead, but Cambridge scored five in a 15-0 run and Ohio State built a 21-8 lead after one quarter and never looked back. Mobley had 15 points off the bench on 6-for-8 shooting by halftime, and Diaz scored 12 as the Buckeyes increased their advantage to 53-25. Reserve Seini Henry made two free throws and a 3-pointer in a 13-13 third quarter and Ohio State led 66-38 heading to the fourth. Ohio State outshot the Knights 54%-30% from the floor with an 8-7 advantage in 3-pointers despite taking 10 fewer shots from distance. Fairleigh Dickinson had to take a 10-hour bus ride from Teaneck, N.J., on Saturday in order to play the game after the FAA grounded all flights on Friday. Up next Fairleigh Dickinson hosts Rider on Tuesday.
